text:
maria: quick sync: i'm exploring a progressive stream-priority approach to soft warmstarts so we can prime hot shards without saturating node IO/ram. want thoughts on backpressure signals and loader API changes.
kevin: nice. high level?
maria: idea: instead of 'stream everything until complete', the loader accepts a priority bucket and a budget (bytes or token window). runtime hands a sequence of (shard_id, priority_bucket, budget_bytes). loader streams up to budget, yields, and runtime can requeue. this keeps priming work bounded per-slot.
ali: sounds reasonable. what backpressure signals do we use to throttle? node-level metrics are noisy.
maria: primaries: io_util_pct, resident_memory_mb, inflight_prime_streams, kv_cache_evictions_per_min. plus route-level tail_latency_change. if any exceed thresholds we slow down or drop low-priority buckets.
dena: for multi-tenant nodes we probably need a fairness rule: each tenant gets N priority units per minute. otherwise one heavy model starves others.
kevin: agree. we should expose token_budget and byte_budget separately to allow quantized formats to behave better. also an optional 'deadline_ms' so loader can prioritize short-critical primes.
ali: loader API sketch (proto-ish):
```
rpc PrepareShardStream(PrepareRequest) returns (PrepareAck) {}
message PrepareRequest { string shard_id = 1; string bucket = 2; uint64 byte_budget = 3; uint64 token_budget = 4; uint32 deadline_ms = 5; map<string,string> hints = 6; }
message PrepareAck { enum Status { ACCEPTED=0; THROTTLED=1; REJECTED=2; } Status status = 1; uint64 accepted_bytes = 2; }
```
maria: exact shape can vary, but the key is bounded deliveries and an explicit ACK so runtime knows how much progressed.
dena: how do we reconcile with existing manifest fields? i don't want to bake too many runtime knobs into manifests. maybe manifest can include 'default_bucket' and 'max_parallel_buckets' only. runtime route config can override per-customer.
kevin: +1. manifest minimal: { default_stream_bucket: "foreground|background|prefetch", max_parallel_buckets: 2 }
ali: for operational safety we need automated degrade triggers. propose: probe baseline p50/p95 per-route; during prime compute p99_ratio = p99_during_prime / baseline_p99. if p99_ratio > 1.25 OR node_io_util > 0.85, then reduce budgets by 50% for low-priority buckets and escalate to full fallback (block warmstart) only if sustained for > 2 minutes.
maria: i like the step-down approach. also want a global circuit breaker: if more than M nodes report > X% eviction_rate while priming, disable soft warmstart cluster-wide for that model_version.
dena: telemetry: need rollups per-model+bucket: bytes_streamed, primes_started, primes_completed, throttles, rejects, p99_ratio, eviction_rate. trace-bot should tag samples with node_id and tenant_id.
kevin: for low-latency detection, sample full request traces when p99_ratio exceeds threshold, mask tokens.
ali: edge case: gzipped safetensors chunks produce bad byte_budget estimates. loader should accept 'estimated_uncompressed_bytes' hint.
maria: good catch. also add hint 'format=compressed|safetensors|mmapped' so runtime can tune budgets.
dena: rollout plan: feature flag behind agent+runtime opt-in. run staging with 10% traffic for a week. collect rollups and compare tail latency and kv cache hit.
maria: next steps: i'll draft a short RFC with the loader API, manifest minimal fields, and degrade rules. ali will prototype the aggregator rollups. kevin will add manifest patch if we agree. dena will own staging canary.
kevin: can you add an example manifest snippet in the RFC?
maria: sure, example:
```
manifest_annotations: {
  "default_stream_bucket": "background",
  "max_parallel_buckets": "2",
  "allow_progressive_stream": "true"
}
```
ali: minor naming nit: prefer `allow_progressive_stream` over `allow_soft_warm` to avoid ambiguity.
dena: +1.
trace-bot: note: api-change: PrepareShardStream proposed. created issue #4287.
maria: i'll open the RFC and link the issue. thanks all.
kevin: :thumbsup:
